entities.summary: Theodore "Fats" Navarro was an American jazz trumpet player and a pioneer of the bebop style of jazz improvisation in the 1940s. A native of Key West, Florida, he toured with big bands before achieving fame as a bebop trumpeter in New York. Following a series of studio sessions with leading bebop figures including Tadd Dameron, Bud Powell, and Kenny Clarke, he became ill with tuberculosis and died at the age of 26. Despite the short duration of his career, he had a strong stylistic influence on trumpet players who rose to fame in later decades, including Miles Davis, Clifford Brown and Lee Morgan.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fats Navarro's innovative trumpet playing had a lasting impact on the development of bebop, influencing notable jazz musicians like Miles Davis and Clifford Brown. His brief career serves as an example of how individual artistic expression can contribute to significant cultural shifts.
